name: Palladian Construction Proprioceptive Lattice Frame
description:
A sub-dermal mesh of piezoelectric filaments and micro-gyroscopic nodes woven through the fascia of the torso, limbs, and cervical spine, the Proprioceptive Lattice Frame continuously triangulates the body's spatial orientation relative to its environment at a resolution of 0.003 degrees. The system feeds a constant low-bandwidth signal to the cerebellum via a hardwired spinal tap, supplementing and refining the body's native proprioceptive sense rather than replacing it. In environments with disrupted vestibular input — extreme vibration, zero-G transit, magnetic interference zones, or the disorienting architecture of certain corporate arcologies — the Frame maintains postural and spatial certainty where biology fails.

What distinguishes it from competitors is the Frame's construction heritage: Palladian's engineers adapted the same load-sensing filament technology used in structural integrity monitoring for megabuilds, miniaturized and re-tensioned for biological substrate. The result is a system that doesn't just track orientation but models stress distribution across the body's skeletal frame in real time, flagging joints under abnormal load before injury occurs. Users report a persistent low-level awareness of their own skeleton — described variously as 'feeling like architecture' or 'knowing exactly where your edges are.'

The Frame is standard-issue for Palladian's own high-altitude and subsurface construction crews, who work in environments where a misjudged step or unexpected platform shift is fatal. Beyond construction, it has found a devoted secondary market among parkour couriers, competitive dancers, and close-quarters combat specialists who prize the Frame's ability to make the body feel geometrically legible to itself.

cultural_context: Among Palladian's workforce, the Frame is a mark of seniority — given to crew leads and structural engineers rather than general laborers, it signals that the company has invested in keeping you alive because you're worth keeping. In the broader GLMZ street culture, 'wearing Palladian' carries an association with physical competence and groundedness, a blue-collar prestige distinct from the sleeker corporate augments. Some users speak of the Frame with an almost spiritual reverence, describing it as making them feel 'present' in their body in a way nothing else does.
known_users: Structural surveyors operating in collapse zones
story_hooks: A Palladian crew lead's Frame begins feeding anomalous stress data — not from her own skeleton, but from the building she's standing in. Someone has wired the structure to collapse on a timer, and she's the only one who can feel it.

A combat specialist with the Frame installed is being hunted by someone who knows the augment's one weakness: it can be spoofed by a targeted low-frequency vibration emitter, flooding the user with false spatial data and inducing sudden, total disorientation.

A black-market installer is offering Frame units pulled from Palladian construction fatalities — still integrated with fragments of the previous user's skeletal stress history. Buyers report phantom sensations of falls they never took.
